full_judgment: 14. But fact remains if such restriction is imposed beyond the "Imambara" area, which is admittedly not the private property of the "Imambara", then question comes whether interference of this court. is required? It is claimed by the respondent No. 9 that such restriction is made only for 1st 10 days in the month of Moharram within the "Imambara" but simultaneously the said respondent also claims that such signboard in the form of notice is put on the 450 meter connecting road which is the private property of Imambara. From the materials on record it appears that the said 450 meter road is claimed by respondent No. 9 to be Imambara's property used as connecting road running towards the "Sultanshi Residential Area" But the petitioner claims that the said road is not the private property of the "Imambara" as appear from Annexures D(2) to the supplementary affidavit filed by the petitioner, which shows that the same is under Khatian No.1 recorded not in the name of Imambara but in the name of the Government of Bangladesh., It further appears that a case is pending before the authority under Rule 30 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Rules which is also admitted by respondent No. 9 as well as by the respondent No.4. On the other hand the respondent No.3 in his report stated that 'no restriction or embargo has been made/ imposed upon any person beyond the area of the "Imambara" area. Thus we are of the view that the temporary sign board, as evident from the photographs (Annexure- B series to the writ petition) captioning সরকারী নির্দেশ মোতাবেক পবিত্র মহরমের নিয়মাবলির প্রতি শ্রদ্ধা জ্ঞাপনর্থে ইমাম বাড়ায় নিজস্ব রাত্তা দিয়ে চলাচলের সময় সকলকে জুতা টুপি ও ছাতা ব্যবহার না করার জন্য অনুরোধ করা হইল। clearly show that the same has been put up beside the road which runs towards the "Sultanshi Residential Area" which is con- fusing. Neither the respondent No.3 nor the respondent No.4 in their reports or in the affidavit admits that the government has given such direction or permission upon the "Muharram Udzapon Committee" to hang/ put up such sign board under the said caption. However, since the signboard if any, is put up on the private property of the respondent No. 9 and since there in no embargo in putting such signboard/notice on the private property the same cannot/does not create any embargo upon the pedestrian generally using the public road running towards "Sultanshi Residential Area", upon wearing caps, shoes and umbrellas. In respect of putting up such sign- board/notice on the 450 meter road immaterial whether the same is claimed to be the private road of the "Imambara" or the same belongs to the government (as appears from Annexure-D(2) to the supplementary affidavit filed by the petitioner showing that the LGED has constructed the said road) and that a miscellaneous case under Rule 30 of the SA &T Rules is pending before the appropriate authority, thus it is clear that there are disputes in respect of the said road/property in question. As such, no such notice or signboard can be put up thereon unless the miscellaneous case under Rules is disposed of or upon finally deciding the title in an appropriate suit by the civil court. However, till finalization of the matter of owner ships of the said road the respondent No.9 or anyone else, cannot under any circumstances, put up such sign board.
